title: The carried low batch of 3.8.0
desiredOutcome: Every low finding carried to BUG-33-gfj is fixed in the code, or answered with the evidence that nothing is left to change, and the bug closes before 3.8.0 is tagged

findings.issue: The wave's new segment matcher treats any segment holding *?[ as a wildcard even when it comes from a files entry, which is a literal path (_task_outputs.covers compares files as plain prefixes). Two tasks in different dynamic-route directories, a common Next.js/SvelteKit/Nuxt layout, are now reported as overlapping and serialised: overlap of files app/[slug]/page.tsx with app/[id]/page.tsx (and with app/s/page.tsx) returns an overlap at HEAD and none at base 8c4bb8bd; the deferral names paths no task shares, and the guide's sentence that covers decides is not what happens for files entries. No case has a files entry with a glob character.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.11-3st (ec36e9abf7dd): Treat a segment as a pattern only when it comes from the outputs half (segments carry an is-pattern flag, always false for files entries, compared literally); a case where the three dynamic-route tasks share one wave, and its twin where an outputs pattern app/*/page.tsx still overlaps files app/[slug]/page.tsx.

findings.issue: restore_copy now settles a copy with nothing to put back and answers restored=None, which restore_tree maps to E_USAGE (exit 2) 'nothing restored', the same exit as a state naming no tree, so an orchestrator reading the exit cannot tell 'dropped, settled, run next' from 'nothing to act on'; un14/un15 never assert the verb's exit.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.13-3st (db8bf3580c85): Report the drop as its own outcome (a dropped field) and have restore_tree exit E_OK with a line saying the copy was dropped and next goes on, keeping E_USAGE for no copy standing; a drive-level case asserting the exit and text.

findings.issue: The no-reviewer-return stop now prints the reviewer brief's submit block, but the no-phase-review-return stop still does not print the phase reviewer brief's, though the same helper would cover it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.13-3st (db8bf3580c85): Route the phase-review stop through the same brief_submit helper, with a case.

findings.issue: The gate-reach check runs inside the manifest index lock (called from _locked_add, _locked_done and _locked_scope between acquire and release). Each call starts the project's listing commands, git ls-files and reads every .py in the tree: measured 5.5 s to 26.6 s per P156 task, where add and done held the lock well under a second before. Another index-lock taker (an executor's file-return in a parallel wave, the panel, another verb) waits WAIT_SECONDS = 5.0 for a live holder and is then refused. In add and scope the result is only printed, so the lock is held for nothing; in add it runs after the write, so an exception in this advisory path would report a successful add as an internal error.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.12-3st (f0042ffc0001): For add and scope compute reach after the lock is released, from the written plan. For done compute it before acquiring the lock from a pre-read, and write the note under the lock only if the task's files and gate are unchanged. Wrap the advisory call fail-open (a 'gate reach not asked: <why>' line). Add a case holding the lock across a slow listing stub and asserting a concurrent note is not refused.

findings.issue: add --from-file, the batch path /audit:phase add uses (commands/phase.md), hands tests.add, tests.gate, files and phase.testGate from the JSON straight to _build_task, never through read_list_flags or joined_entry_parts. Verified in a scratch repo: a batch task with tests.add ['tests/test_a.py,tests/test_b.py'] stores that one joined entry and adds the bogus path to files - the defect the shared reader was meant to close; a joined testGate or tests.gate in a batch only gets the validator's warning.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.14-3st (36deecd80070): Run each batch list field (files, tests.add, tests.gate, phase.testGate, dependsOn, blockedBy) through the same per-reading predicate in the batch problem checks, using joined_entry_parts with the plan's buildCommands keys for gates; refuse a joined value with the field path; add batch cases mirroring the flag refusal cases, and extend the argparse-walk case (or a sibling) to walk the batch keys too.

findings.issue: For free-text entries the each-part-is-an-entry predicates accept the tail of a sentence, so legitimate single entries are refused: `--tests-add "tests/test_x.py: reads _config.py, _deps.py"` and `--accept-open "R1=threshold n=3, m=4 is fine"` are refused, and the suggested repeated form would store a wrong entry.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.14-3st (36deecd80070): Tighten to whole-entry shapes: after a `<path>: <text>` part, a later part counts only if it also opens with `<path>:`; for accept-open and carried the key half must have the plan's finding-id shape. Allow cases for both probed values.

findings.issue: --gate-drop gets the joined-value refusal although it names an entry already held and stores nothing, so a legacy joined entry such as `lint,test` cannot be dropped (scope and retarget both refuse); the refusal says the value would be stored and suggests drops of entries the gate does not hold.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.14-3st (36deecd80070): Skip the joined check for a gate-drop value equal to an entry the gate holds (or leave gate_drop to _retarget_gate_now's held/not-held reading); a case dropping a legacy joined entry.

findings.issue: The gate-reach fact gathering is a second hand copy of run-test-gate's _affected_facts and has already drifted: plain subprocess.run with no process group (a timed-out listing's children outlive the verb) and different timeouts. A later change to the facts run-test-gate gathers silently changes only one answer.
findings.resolution: fixed in P156.12-3st (f0042ffc0001): Move the fact gathering, shell runner with group teardown included, into one shared helper both may import per _deps.LAYERS; have run-test-gate's affected steps and the gate-reach check call it; delete the copy.

findings.issue: The step-pointer lint matches only lowercase step/steps, so this codebase's uppercase docstring style escapes it, and two stale pointers survive: audit-task.py:5292 ('reference/orchestrator.md's STEP 2', the promote step is execute-task.md's step 2) and :7798 ('orchestrator.md's STEP 4 ... 4b ... 4c', which orchestrator.md does not hold). The lint's WHAT IT CANNOT SEE does not name case.
findings.resolution: Match the step word case-insensitively; repoint both pointers to reference/execute-task.md; an sp case with an uppercase STEP 4c pointer to a document lacking it.

findings.file: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py (wave tree records); tests/test_drive_phase.py wt2, wt4, wt6, wt6r
findings.issue: Release-tier CI run 41853969220 at 59e4a5f8 is red on every windows selftests leg: test_drive_phase wt2, wt4, wt6 and wt6r fail because the tree the drive records for a wave member, and dispatches in, is now '\\trees\\drive-wave-P1.1' where the tree verb handed back '/trees/drive-wave-P1.1'. The native spelling meant for messages reached the stored record, so on Windows the state no longer holds what the tree verb answered.
findings.resolution: Keep the tree verb's answer verbatim in every record and dispatch; apply the native spelling only where a path is shown to a human. Prove it under a Windows-shaped path module (ntpath) on posix so the case is red here before the fix.

findings.issue: Release-tier CI run 41853969220 at 59e4a5f8: test__config st8 fails on the windows cp1252 leg. In a bare repository the timed-out first question is followed by a second ask with a 0.012 s remaining budget, which then times out too; on posix the same case is green.
findings.resolution: Find whether this is the case's timing assumption (a remaining budget a Windows git cannot meet) or the code asking again; fix whichever is wrong so the case holds on any runner, and say which it was.

findings.issue: Without --verbose the short output keeps only warnings naming the written task id, so every WARNING: gate reach: line (it names a path) is dropped and an operator running add, scope or done from the command line never sees a reach warning; the suites pass --verbose to see them.
findings.resolution: Keep every warning the verb itself raised about the task it wrote in the short output (or say in the clipped line that warnings were held back and how to print them), with a case running add without --verbose.

It places a `check` clause, `cd <tree> && git apply --reverse --check <patch>`, the check the patch can answer alone. I checked that command in a scratch repo: exit 0 over a tree that holds the work, exit 1 over one that lacks it. (R2) drive_locked's set-aside branch now takes `--answer decline`: for a decision set aside because a task can run, answer_refusal is asked first and refuses before the pending decision is dropped, so a decline with no --reason leaves the decision there for a second try with words. P155-R14 fixed both ways: the pin is kept for a blocked task (sd18), and a stop whose pin is gone names no deleted ref (ar6g). P155-R15 fixed by sd17, a cancelled task whose patch stands, so the status arm decides alone; probed with `return not patch_stands` (m1, red). outcome.technical: P155-R23 (restore_copy's two refusals saying 'the next move drops it'): fixed by the finding's resolution, not by rewording alone - a reworded refusal would describe a dead end, since unsettled_stop stops dispatch and integration over a standing copy before any move runs. _worktrees.restore_copy now settles both shapes the way _resume does: a copy with no index.json is dropped (new _dropped helper: restored None, the error saying the copy was dropped and the tree is settled; a drop that fails stays restored False with the copy kept); the copy of a move the marker recorded (base == end) goes to new _settle_recorded, which drops it when _newer_work over heads (end,) names nothing and otherwise keeps it naming every diverging path and saying no move, restore, dispatch or integration takes it down over newer work. The base-not-in-(start,end) refusal is unchanged. Cases un14 (no index.json dropped, tree_unsettled False after, no byte changed, HEAD at base), un15 (recorded move copy dropped, HEAD at head), un16 (over-fire twin: recorded move with newer work kept, a.txt and c.txt named, no byte changed, no 'next move' in the text). drive-phase restore_tree renders restored None as before ('nothing restored - <error>', E_USAGE), so the drop reads through it unchanged. P155-R60 (ut5's first-site and every-caller rules had no failing case): added ut6 (planted twice(): removal, tree_unsettled, second removal: named; its twin once() asking before both: not named) and ut7 (planted remover() with callers asks_first and asks_after: named; twin covered() whose two callers both ask first: not named). These two cases pass on HEAD by construction because the scanner lives in the test file. tasks.description: Fix P156-R2 and P156-R3 (docs/audit/phases/P156.json review.findings). R3: the no-phase-review-return stop goes through the same brief_submit helper the reviewer stop uses; a case.

outcome.technical: R2: _worktrees.restore_copy's answer gains a `dropped` field (False by default; `_dropped` sets it True when the drop left nothing beside the tree, read off the disk through _with_kept), so a drop is its own outcome apart from the `restored` None a missing copy answers. drive-phase.restore_tree answers a drop with E_OK and '<prefix> <phase>: the copy beside <tree> was dropped - <why>; `next` goes on from here', keeping E_USAGE 'nothing restored' for a state with no tree and a tree with no copy. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's _worktrees and drive-phase sections name the new outcome (un17, uv3, uv4) and the phase stop (ur5, ur6). tasks.title: Every batch list field goes through the shared list reader, and the reader refuses only real joins
tasks.description: Fix P156-R5, P156-R6 and P156-R7 (docs/audit/phases/P156.json review.findings). R5: add --from-file passes files, tests.add, tests.gate, phase.testGate, dependsOn and blockedBy to the task builder without the shared reader, so a joined entry is still stored; run each batch list field through the same per-reading predicate and extend the walk case to the batch keys. R6: the each-part-is-an-entry predicates refuse legitimate prose entries (a tests-add description with a comma, an accept-open reason with an `=`); tighten to whole-entry shapes with allow cases. R7: --gate-drop must be able to drop a legacy joined entry the gate holds; a case.

outcome.technical: audit-task.py: the per-part predicates became whole-value readings (_ENTRY_READINGS maps reading -> joined-parts function); new joined_parts(reading, value, build_keys) is the one answer read_list_flags and the batch both ask. R6: tests-add reads through the new _manifest_phases.joined_tests_add_parts (each part a whole entry: once a part is `<path>: <text>`, a later part must open with `<path>:`); pair keys must have the finding-id shape `<x>-<letters><n>` (measured over every review finding id in docs/audit, examples and tests: all fit; the R-only `_FINDING_ID` would have missed hand-recorded T/S ids); waiver paths must name a file (tests_add_path). Tightening only narrows what is refused, so nothing legal before the phase is refused now. R7: gate_drop gets a new reading `held` (values as given, never refused at read); _retarget_gate_now's not-held refusal now appends the per-entry spelling via _held_drop_spelling when the value joins entries the gate holds; --gate-drop help no longer claims the refusal. R5: batch_list_fields() derives [(path, reading)] from BATCH_FLAG_KEYS + PHASE_KEY_DESTS + LIST_FLAG_READINGS (tasks[].files/dependsOn/blockedBy/fixes split, tasks[].tests.add tests-add, tasks[].tests.gate and phase.testGate gate, phase.blockedBy split); _batch_joined_problems refuses any item reading as several entries under its field's reading, named by field path (tasks[0].tests.add); batch_problems(doc, build_keys) and read_batch(..., keys_for) take the plan's buildCommands keys through _gate_build_keys(args, batch_gate_items(doc)), read only when a gate item holds a comma. Docs: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (_manifest_phases and audit-task sections) and verbs-in-full.md (list-flag paragraph, --gate-drop, the batch refusal list). Tests: lr3 gains the `held` branch and _LR_SAMPLES a held row; new lr8-lr11, lb1-lb3 in tests/test_audit_task.py (lr-block 14/14), jp2 in tests/test__manifest_phases.py (146/146). Mutations, each in a throwaway copy of the tree under the scratchpad (never in the task tree): gate_drop back to `gate` -> lr10 red; pair regex loosened -> lr8; waiver one-word -> lr8; batch check removed -> lb1, lb2; build keys not passed to the batch -> lb2; held hint off -> lr11; described rule removed -> jp2 + lr8; over-fire (any comma joins) -> lr6, lr8, lb3; all restored by discarding the copy. Dependants: full-gate.py, run-test-gate.py, _affected_tests.py, _gate_derive.py, _scoped_commit.py, derive-phase-gate.py, drive-phase.py, _manifest_rules.py still correct - they use names this change does not touch (joined_entry_parts unchanged, _is_list_operator, gate_entry_commands untouched); their suites and every importer suite (test__invariants, test_close_phase, test_commit_task_work, test__scoped_commit, test__doctor_trail, test__filed_returns, test__config, test__deps, test__output_lints, test_drive_phase, test_repair_tests_add, test__manifest_rules) pass in the full sweep.
